findings.title: Retriable-failure branch parks a timer but nothing actually redrives — leads stall forever
findings.evidence: On status=failed + is_retriable, orchestrator registers a 5-min timer and emits NO transition, commenting 'Muscle will redrive.' But main.rs processes each command exactly once and commits (no redrive logic anywhere in the muscle). on_timer just clears pending_state. So a transient external failure (Apify 5xx, rate limit) -> lead doesn't advance, timer clears, command never re-runs -> lead silently stalls. The retry contract is documented but unimplemented.
findings.recommendation: Implement actual redrive: either the orchestrator re-emits the original command to outreach.commands on the timer, or the muscle re-queues on retriable failure, or drop the retriable concept and route everything to on_error. Pick one and make it real.
findings.fix: orchestrator retriable branch parks a real __retry__ transition + bounded retry counter (3 per lead/node); on_timer emits it; transition_worker re-fires the SAME source node. Exhausted retries route to on_error.

findings.title: THEME: the system has no working retry/redrive at any stage — failures are logged and dropped
findings.evidence: Three independently-verified findings compose into one architectural gap: EXEC-001 (dispatcher/transitions auto-commit + catch-and-continue -> failed events never retried), PROJ-001 (failed projection archived-as-seen, never rebuilt), FLINK-001 (retriable failure parks a dead timer, muscle never redrives). At every plane — ingest, project, orchestrate — a transient failure silently strands the work. For a lead-gen product this means leads/contacts/scores can vanish on any blip with no recovery and no alert.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one coherent failure policy: manual-commit-after-success + dead-letter topic for poison, idempotent reprocessing, and a real redrive path. This is the single highest-leverage reliability fix and should precede shipping templates to customers.
findings.fix: Coherent failure policy adopted: bus.consume_forever does manual commit-after-success + dead-letters poison records (outreach.dead_letter); dispatcher + transitions switched to enable_auto_commit=False + earliest + commit=True; projector now projects-before-archive (PROJ-001); Flink redrive made real (FLINK-001).

findings.title: SSRF guard is string-prefix based and bypassable
findings.evidence: is_blocked_host does string matching (starts_with '127.', '10.', '169.254.169.254', etc.). Bypassable via decimal IP (http://2130706433/ = 127.0.0.1), IPv6-mapped ([::ffff:127.0.0.1]), octal/hex encodings, or DNS rebinding (hostname resolving to 169.254.169.254). Coverage IS correct — verified only webhook.rs + http_call.rs take operator URLs and BOTH call validate_outbound_url; enrich/transform/leadgen/apify/serper hit fixed provider URLs. So residual risk is the guard's porousness, not skipped calls. The code comment self-acknowledges the gap. Also h.starts_with('172.2') over-blocks 172.200.x / 172.2.x (false positives).
findings.recommendation: Resolve host -> IP and reject any IP in non-public ranges using std::net::IpAddr classification (is_loopback/is_private/is_link_local), not string prefixes. Optionally pin DNS resolution to block rebinding.
findings.fix: common.rs validate_outbound_url is async + IP-classification based: IP literals classified directly, hostnames resolved via tokio lookup_host and rejected if ANY resolved IP is loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/ULA. Callers awaited.

findings.title: Fernet key derived by unsalted single-pass SHA-256 of SECRET_KEY; rotation orphans ciphertext
findings.evidence: _raw = hashlib.sha256(secret_key.encode()).digest() then Fernet(b64(_raw)). Deterministic, unsalted, no KDF/context. Not a practical break given SECRET_KEY entropy (64 hex), but not best-practice key derivation (HKDF with context/salt is conventional). Also: rotating SECRET_KEY makes decrypt() raise InvalidToken for ALL existing connection ciphertext (credential_refs, omni_connections) — rotation isn't a config swap, it orphans every stored secret. Relates to the project's 'rotate secrets' note.
findings.recommendation: Use HKDF(secret_key, info='omni-connection-encryption') for derivation. Document/handle SECRET_KEY rotation as a re-encrypt migration, not a config change.
findings.fix: encryption.py derives the Fernet key with HKDF-SHA256 (info=omni-connection-encryption); MultiFernet keeps the legacy SHA-256 key as a decrypt-only fallback so existing ciphertext still decrypts and rotates forward on next write.

ALSO this file is in the dead-service cluster (0 callers) — so currently moot, but if revived, escape per-context. Substitution also loops dict order so a value containing {{otherkey}} can double-substitute.
findings.recommendation: If revived: context-aware escaping (HTML-escape for email bodies), single-pass substitution. Otherwise delete with SVC-002.

findings.evidence: require_muscle compares `authorization.removeprefix('Bearer ').strip() != expected` with Python !=, which short-circuits on first differing byte -> timing side-channel on MUSCLE_SHARED_SECRET. The module already imports `secrets` (line 21).

findings.title: 'one-shot' credential ref is actually multi-read until expiry/release
findings.evidence: redeem_credential sets redeemed_at = COALESCE(redeemed_at, NOW()) — records first redemption but does NOT block subsequent redemptions. A ref is redeemable repeatedly for its 600s TTL or until released. Docs/comments call it 'one-shot'. (The Apify multi-step handler actually NEEDS re-reads, so behaviour may be intended — but it contradicts the stated contract and widens the leak window.)
findings.recommendation: Either enforce true one-shot (reject if redeemed_at set, and have multi-step handlers cache in-process), or update docs to 'short-TTL, multi-read until released'.
findings.fix: redeem_credential docstring corrected to the real semantics (short-TTL, multi-read until released/expired); multi-step handlers re-read within TTL by design; redeemed_at is observability-only.

findings.title: POST /events lets any authed user inject arbitrary event_types into the durable log
findings.evidence: append_event accepts any event_type/entity_type/payload and publishes to omni.events with no allowlist. The projector then faithfully applies it: a user could publish contact.created, ai.score.completed, lead.sequence_ended, etc. and fabricate projected state. Scoped to their own workspace_id (from auth ctx), so blast radius is their tenant — but within it, arbitrary projected-state forgery (e.g. fake lead scores) is possible.
findings.recommendation: Allowlist user-publishable event_types (e.g. only crm.* mutations a human should author), or route human-authored mutations through typed endpoints instead of raw event injection. Keep internal event_types (ai.*, lead.sequence_ended, *.completed) producible only by workers.
findings.fix: POST /events allowlists user-publishable event_types (CRM mutations + note.added); worker-only events are rejected 403.

findings.fix: create_connection catches asyncpg.UniqueViolationError specifically for the 409; other DB errors surface as 500.

findings.title: auth_google's 2 unauthenticated routes are the unavoidable OAuth handshake (clean)
findings.evidence: RESOLVED by full read of auth_google.py. The two routes are exactly the OAuth bootstrap: POST /auth/google/login (returns the Google authorize URL — must be anonymous, the user IS signing in) and GET /auth/google/callback (Google's redirect target — exchanges code, upserts user, sets JWT cookie). CSRF is defended via a server-side _STATE_STORE with 10min TTL bound to each /login (callback rejects unknown/stale state). email_verified is checked. system_scope wraps the pre-workspace upsert. JWT cookie is httponly+secure+SameSite=Lax. Nothing sensitive is exposed — the missing auth dep is correct by construction.
findings.recommendation: No action. The two anonymous routes are unavoidable OAuth and leak nothing.

findings.title: ai.score + ai.classify appear in the canvas palette but silently no-op when wired into a flow
findings.evidence: Both are registered nodes (seen in the Playwright canvas palette: 'score','classify') so a user can drag+wire them. But NODE_CHANNEL (commands.py:33-60) has no 'ai.score' or 'ai.classify' key, and ChannelType (core/events.py:19) has no SCORE/CLASSIFY variant. So when fired from a canvas flow, dispatcher._channel_for returns None -> 'not a muscle channel; no command' -> the queued event is dropped, node never executes. They only run via the AI Studio POST /ai/jobs path (ai_studio.py). compose/enrich/screen_company/screen_person ARE in NODE_CHANNEL and work on canvas; score/classify do not.
findings.recommendation: Either add ai.score/ai.classify to NODE_CHANNEL + a ChannelType + muscle handler so they work on canvas, OR remove them from the canvas registry (keep them AI-Studio-only) so the palette doesn't offer non-functional nodes.

findings.title: A transient projection failure permanently skips the projection (archive says 'seen' forever)
findings.evidence: _handle: _archive_event INSERTs (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, returns inserted), then `if inserted: _apply_projection`, then _record_offset, then consumer.commit(). If archive succeeds but _apply_projection throws (transient DB error), consume_forever catches it and skips commit -> record redelivered. On redelivery _archive_event hits ON CONFLICT -> inserted=False -> _apply_projection is SKIPPED. Net: event durably archived but its projection (contact/company/lead/score/ai_job) is never built. Read the whole _handle + _archive_event + consume_forever to confirm.
findings.recommendation: Make archive + projection + offset one atomic unit, or drive _apply_projection off the archive row's presence independent of `inserted`, or only archive AFTER projection succeeds. Don't gate projection on first-insert.
findings.fix: projector/main.py _handle applies the projection BEFORE archiving and commits after. Projections are idempotent upserts, so redelivery re-applies safely; the archive row is the durable 'projected' commit-point. No longer gated on first-insert.

findings.title: _project_message keys on event id; other projectors key on entity_id (inconsistent)
findings.evidence: Messages INSERT with id=env['id'] (the event id) + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, whereas contact/company/deal/lead use entity_id with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Messages are therefore append-only and can't be corrected by a later event. Likely intentional but inconsistent with the rest of the projection model.
findings.recommendation: Document the append-only intent in the function, or align if message correction is ever needed.
findings.fix: Documented the append-only intent of _project_message (keys on event id; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is redelivery idempotency; no correction path).

findings.title: Auto-commit + catch-and-continue = silent event loss (at-most-once)
findings.evidence: dispatcher.py:160 and transition_worker.py:499 set enable_auto_commit=True. bus.consume_forever (bus.py:171) catches handler exceptions and continues. aiokafka auto-commits offsets on its timer regardless of handler success, so a transient handler failure (DB blip, Kafka publish error) commits the offset and the event is NEVER retried. Read whole: the docstrings claim at-least-once but the wiring is at-most-once. For the dispatcher a dropped command = a lead silently stuck.
findings.recommendation: Switch dispatcher + transitions to manual commit AFTER successful handling (commit in on_record like the projector), or move failed records to a dead-letter topic before the offset advances.
findings.fix: bus.consume_forever commit=True does manual commit-after-success and dead-letters a poison record before advancing; dispatcher+transitions use it with enable_auto_commit=False.

findings.title: _skip_current_batch advances ONE offset, not the whole batch
findings.evidence: After a failed getmany() (codec error), consumer.position(tp) returns the batch start. Seeking pos+1 advances by a single offset, but a compressed Kafka batch holds many records, so a poison batch of N needs N failed iterations to clear — log-spamming each. The docstring/comment claims it 'skips the batch'. Self-heals but the reasoning is wrong. (Self-introduced this session.)
findings.recommendation: On codec failure, seek to the high-watermark of the failed partition (or end) rather than pos+1, and log once. Or surface the poison offset to a dead-letter and skip past the whole batch via committed+1 of the next fetchable batch.
findings.fix: _skip_current_batch seeks each partition to its high-watermark (end_offsets) instead of pos+1, stepping past the whole poison batch.

findings.title: Dead `commit` parameter on consume_forever
findings.evidence: All three callers verified: dispatcher + transitions use enable_auto_commit=True (no manual commit), projector passes on_record and commits inside it. commit=True is never passed. The commit branch (bus.py:173) is dead. (Self-introduced this session.)
findings.recommendation: Remove the commit param (and its branch), or actually use it for the dispatcher/transitions manual-commit fix from EXEC-001.
findings.fix: The commit parameter is now load-bearing — drives the manual commit-after-success path used by dispatcher+transitions.

findings.title: Redundant exception clause `except (KafkaError, Exception)`
findings.evidence: Exception is a superclass of KafkaError, so naming both is redundant and misleading. ruff/flake8 would flag. (Self-introduced this session.)
findings.recommendation: Reduce to `except Exception` with a comment, or catch the specific codec/Kafka errors explicitly.
findings.fix: Reduced except (KafkaError, Exception) to except Exception and removed the unused KafkaError import.

findings.title: publish_events is not atomic (partial fan-out on crash)
findings.evidence: publish_events loops send_and_wait per envelope (bus.py:90-96). If a node emits N intent events and the process dies mid-loop, some publish and some don't, with no rollback. Used by _fire_node (transition_worker.py:378) when a node emits multiple events. Low likelihood (single fast producer) but real.
findings.recommendation: Use the producer's transactional API (begin/commit) for multi-event publishes, or make node multi-event emission idempotent + replayable.
findings.fix: publish_events non-atomicity left as-is: the documented policy is at-least-once with idempotent projection upserts + dead-letter, which tolerates partial fan-out via redelivery. Full Kafka transactions deferred as not load-bearing under the new policy.

findings.title: ExecutionResult Pydantic model drifts from the real wire format
findings.evidence: events.py ExecutionResult has no lead_id and no metadata field, but the actual result envelope (muscle output + _emit_synthetic_result at transition_worker.py:389) carries both lead_id and metadata{workspace_id,node_id,next_handle}. The model is stale documentation; the hot path uses hand-built dicts, so nothing validates result envelopes against a schema.
findings.recommendation: Either align ExecutionResult to the real wire shape and validate inbound results against it, or delete the unused models to avoid them misleading readers.
findings.fix: Removed the drifted ActionCommand/ExecutionResult/LeadContext/StateTransition models from core/events.py (never imported). Kept the live enums; documented the canonical dict wire shape.

findings.title: for_each / join fan-out core is sound
findings.evidence: Read whole: cycle guard (ancestor walk MAX_ANCESTOR_WALK_DEPTH + per-root descendant cap via recursive CTE + per-fanout clamp), the join barrier uses an atomic UPDATE ... fanout_done=fanout_done+1 RETURNING (transition_worker.py:310) so concurrent child arrivals can't double-count, and max_items=0 is honoured literally. This is the most robust part of the codebase.
findings.recommendation: No action. This is the reference standard for the rest.

findings.title: No Cargo.lock committed + Dockerfile builds on nightly
findings.evidence: Confirmed no Cargo.lock in repo. Dockerfile FROM rustlang/rust:nightly-bookworm-slim. A fresh `cargo generate-lockfile` on stable 1.83 pulled hashbrown 0.17.1 (requires edition2024) via indexmap 2.14.0 -> h2 -> reqwest, proving deps float forward and break clean rebuilds.
findings.recommendation: Commit a Cargo.lock the prod image resolves; pin Dockerfile to a dated nightly OR pin transitive deps for stable. Avoid over-engineering the transitive tree.
findings.fix: rust-toolchain.toml pinned to stable 1.89.0 (off nightly); Dockerfile FROM rust:1.89-bookworm with cargo build --release --locked; Cargo.lock committed; removed Dockerfile.local.

findings.title: Dead canvas-editor code in the Campaigns LIST page
findings.evidence: App.tsx routes /campaigns -> <Campaigns/> (no :id) and /campaigns/:id -> <CampaignEditor/>. Campaigns/index.tsx reads useParams().id (always undefined at /campaigns) and has full canvas state (useNodesState/useGetGraph/useCanvasHistory) + imports components/Canvas|Panels|Sidebar. Playwright PROOF: /campaigns renders a list of campaign cards (no canvas); /campaigns/:id renders CampaignEditor with the real ReactFlow canvas. The canvas code in Campaigns/index.tsx is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Strip canvas state + imports from Campaigns/index.tsx (make it a pure list page); delete the unused components/Canvas|Panels|Sidebar subtree. Verify tsc+eslint stay green and /campaigns still lists.

findings.title: components/Canvas|Panels|Sidebar subtree is dead-at-runtime but live-at-import (~2430 LOC)
findings.evidence: Traced: the subtree is imported ONLY by Campaigns/index.tsx (lines 59-65), and ONLY by that file's canvas-editor code path which is unreachable (route /campaigns never passes :id; the editor is CampaignEditor at /campaigns/:id — Playwright-confirmed). So tsc/eslint see live imports (it compiles), but at runtime none of it renders. Removable, but NOT in isolation: must FIRST strip the dead canvas code + these 7 imports from Campaigns/index.tsx (FE-001), THEN delete the subtree, else the build breaks. Corrected from SUSPECTED after full route + Playwright trace.

findings.title: Node discovery swallows import failures silently
findings.evidence: discover() wraps importlib.import_module in `except Exception: log.exception(...)` then continues. A malformed node disappears from the registry at startup with only a log line — no hard failure in dev.
findings.recommendation: Re-raise in non-prod (env flag) or surface failed-node list in /health so a broken node is loud during development (the extension path we're about to use heavily).
findings.fix: Node discovery records import failures (re-raises when NODE_DISCOVERY_STRICT set); /health surfaces them in node_import_failures and flips to degraded.

findings.title: No hardcoded secrets in app source; no SQL injection
findings.evidence: Grep for sk-ant/api_token/password=literal/SECRET_KEY=hex across backend/app + frontend/src returned nothing. SQL uses asyncpg $1 parameterization throughout; no f-string/format/% interpolation into execute/fetch found. Secrets live in compose/env (known, separate finding for rotation).
findings.recommendation: No action. Maintain the parameterized-query + env-secret discipline.

findings.title: THEME: 8+ palette-visible nodes are dead-on-arrival; the synthetic-result fallback strands any event-emitting non-muscle node
findings.evidence: VERIFIED by reading transition_worker._fire_node (line 382) directly: a node advances ONLY if it is a muscle channel (node_type in NODE_CHANNEL) OR it emitted zero events (`NODE_CHANNEL.get(node_type) is None AND result.events == []`). A node that emits an intent event but is NOT in NODE_CHANNEL gets neither a muscle command nor a synthetic result -> the lead STALLS silently (no error, no advance). The event-contract agent enumerated every node; I spot-verified source/apollo.py (emits source.apollo.requested, node_type source.apollo absent from NODE_CHANNEL, no Rust handler) and the _fire_node guard. Affected DEAD-ON-ARRIVAL nodes (palette-visible, silently do nothing): ai.score, ai.classify (NODE-001), source.apollo, source.hunter, source.proxycurl, source.sheets, source.producthunt (no ChannelType, unlike the WIRED source.linkedin_jobs/source.serper_people/source.serper). This is the same failure CLASS as RETRY-THEME but on the happy path.
findings.recommendation: Decide per node: WIRE it (add node_type->ChannelType + Rust handler, like Apify/Serper) or REMOVE it from the registry so the palette never offers a non-functional node. Separately, make _fire_node loud: if a fired node neither routes to a muscle nor emits a synthetic result, log an error / mark the lead errored instead of silently stalling.
findings.fix: transition_worker._fire_node classifies a non-muscle node's emitted events (projection_only/routable_intent/dead_on_arrival) and ERRORS the lead loudly on an unroutable intent instead of stalling silently. Genuinely-dead source/ai canvas nodes removed from the registry. audit contract test now GREEN.

findings.title: crm.hot_lead_alert advertises 'Alert dispatched' but never sends anything
findings.evidence: Agent-traced + cross-checked against commands.py + dispatcher._is_intent: crm.hot_lead_alert's node_type IS in NODE_CHANNEL (-> HOT_LEAD_ALERT) but the node emits event_type 'lead.hot_alert', which does NOT end in .queued/.requested, so dispatcher._is_intent rejects it BEFORE node_type is ever consulted -> no command -> no Slack/alert. The HOT_LEAD_ALERT muscle channel is an orphaned handler (unreachable). The node also advances the lead via _project_lead writing nothing useful. Same shape applies to crm.add_tag (emits contact.tag_added) and crm.remove_tag (emits contact.tag_removed): both are in NODE_CHANNEL but their event_types fail _is_intent, so ADD_TAG/REMOVE_TAG are also orphaned handlers.
findings.recommendation: Make these three nodes emit .queued intent event_types (e.g. crm.hot_lead_alert.queued) so _is_intent passes and node_type routing fires, OR drop the NODE_CHANNEL entries and implement them as projection-only mutations. Either way, align the emitted event_type suffix with the routing intent.
findings.fix: crm.hot_lead_alert/add_tag/remove_tag emit .queued intent event_types so dispatcher._is_intent passes and node_type routing reaches the muscle handlers.

findings.title: Tags are never persisted -> condition.has_tag is permanently false
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: add_tag/remove_tag emit contact.tag_added/contact.tag_removed (entity_type contact) which hit projector _project_contact. But _project_contact's upsert writes only identity columns (email/first_name/last_name/company/...) and there is NO tags column write — the payload {tag: ...} is silently discarded. condition.has_tag reads custom_fields.tags, which nothing ever writes, so any tag-gated branch always takes 'false'. Two bugs compound: the tag write is lost (CONTRACT-002 routing) AND even the projection path drops it.
findings.recommendation: Add a tags projection (either a tags column / join table on omni_contacts written by _project_contact on tag events, or store on omni_leads.custom_fields.tags). Make condition.has_tag read the same location.
findings.fix: tags persisted: _apply_lead_mutations applies add_tag/remove_tag (from the muscle lead_mutations) into omni_leads.custom_fields.tags set-wise; condition.has_tag already reads that location.

findings.title: crm.create_task emits task.created which NO projector handles (orphaned emitter) + lead stalls
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: create_task emits event_type task.created (entity_type task). The projector's _PROJECTORS / _apply_projection has no 'task' entity branch and there is no omni_tasks projection table -> the event is archived but never projected (pure orphaned emitter). Additionally, like all CRM create/update nodes (create_contact->contact.created, create_deal->deal.created, update_deal->deal.stage_changed), it emits events but isn't in NODE_CHANNEL, so per CONTRACT-001 the lead STALLS after the (for create_task, non-existent) projection.
findings.recommendation: Add a task projection (omni_tasks table + projector branch) and resolve the stall via the CONTRACT-001 fix. Audit all four crm.create_*/update_* nodes together.
findings.fix: crm.create_task is projection-only (advances locally); added omni_tasks table (migration 026) + projector _project_task on task.created. crm.create_contact/create_deal/update_deal also resolved as projection_only by the CONTRACT-001 _fire_node fix.

findings.title: flow.human_approval parks a lead but nothing projects the approval and approval.resolved has no emitter
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: human_approval emits approval.requested (passes _is_intent via .requested suffix) but node_type flow.human_approval is not in NODE_CHANNEL -> no command, and result.events != [] -> no synthetic result -> lead parks/stalls. The docstring claims it 'Surfaces in the Approvals queue' but no projector branch consumes approval.requested (no approvals table). The resume event approval.resolved has NO emitter anywhere in the codebase, so a parked lead can never be resumed by the documented mechanism. flow.goal (lead.goal_reached) and flow.end (lead.sequence_ended) share the terminal-stall shape: they never mark the lead completed via a transition.
findings.recommendation: Implement an approvals projection + a resolve endpoint that emits approval.resolved and re-fires the lead; or remove the node until the approvals plane exists. For flow.goal/flow.end, route the terminal advance explicitly (mark lead completed) rather than relying on a synthetic result that never fires.
findings.fix: flow.human_approval PARKS (NodeResult.park=True -> lead status=waiting, no advance) instead of returning handle=approved. Added omni_approvals table+projector and POST /approvals/{id}/resolve which emits approval.resolved + a transition off the node chosen handle to un-park the lead.

findings.title: condition.replied is hardcoded false with no orchestrator override in code
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: condition.replied returns handle 'false' unconditionally; a comment claims the orchestrator overrides it, but no such override exists in transition_worker (the synthetic-result path uses the node's returned handle verbatim) or orchestrator.py. So a reply-gated branch always takes the no-reply path. Pairs with condition.has_tag (always false, CONTRACT-003).
findings.recommendation: Either implement the reply check (read inbound message projection) or remove the node. Don't ship a condition node that silently always evaluates one way.
findings.fix: condition.replied evaluates against the contact most-recent inbound message: the worker injects last_inbound_at (from omni_messages) into the lead context and the node returns true/false against the window.

findings.title: correlation_id is dropped for every condition/flow node -> trace forks at the next node
findings.evidence: Agent-traced + confirmed against _emit_synthetic_result (line 386-404): the function RECEIVES correlation_id as a parameter but its emitted metadata is only {workspace_id, node_id, next_handle} — correlation_id is omitted. So any transition produced by a non-muscle node carries correlation_id=None (orchestrator _safe_get returns None at line 109). The next node fired off that transition hits `ctx.correlation_id or str(uuid.uuid4())` (every node, e.g. email.py:58) and MINTS A NEW identity. Any workflow with a condition/split/delay/flow node in the path forks its trace there. Combined with commands.py:134 (build_command mints a fresh correlation_id when the dispatcher passes None) the run identity forks at multiple points.
findings.recommendation: Add correlation_id to _emit_synthetic_result's metadata dict (the value is already in scope). Replace `or str(uuid.uuid4())` mints at commands.py:134 with a hard requirement or carry correlation_id on the lead row so it can't be lost.
findings.fix: _emit_synthetic_result includes correlation_id in metadata, so condition/flow/synthetic transitions carry the run identity forward instead of forking the trace.

findings.title: Trace tool can't see the muscle round-trip — outreach.results/transitions are never archived
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: trace.py reads ONLY omni_events_archive, which the projector populates exclusively from omni.events. The post-muscle stream (outreach.results -> Flink -> outreach.transitions -> transition_worker) is never published back to omni.events except when _fire_node runs a NEW node that emits intent. So the muscle's verdict (sent/failed/rate_limited) is never archived; the trace shows only what each node REQUESTED, never the muscle outcome. The tool's own docstring (line 22-23) admits this 'Known gap'. The orchestrator line-109 correlation fix keeps the id alive on the wire, but nothing on that wire is written where trace.py looks.
findings.recommendation: Archive outreach.results (and/or transitions) into omni_events_archive (a second projector consumer or have the transition_worker emit a result.observed event to omni.events) so the trace spine includes the muscle round-trip. Pairs with DATAFLOW-001 (fix the fork first, else the archived ids won't stitch).
findings.fix: Trace-spine gap (muscle round-trip not archived) is a tracing enhancement, not a correctness bug. DATAFLOW-001 (the fork) is fixed; archiving outreach.results is a separate observability feature deferred.

findings.title: workspace_id is trusted from the muscle's echoed metadata without re-validation
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: orchestrator copies workspace_id verbatim from the muscle's echoed metadata (orchestrator.py:104) into the transition; transition_worker uses meta.get('workspace_id') (line 436) directly in every WHERE workspace_id=$N query and only re-derives from the lead when ABSENT, never cross-checking a PRESENT value against omni_leads.workspace_id for the given lead_id. Today low-risk because the muscle clones metadata verbatim (common.rs) and a mismatched workspace_id yields zero rows (RLS + workspace-scoped lead lookup) rather than cross-tenant writes — so it fails safe, but by accident of the query shape, not by an explicit assert. Anything that can publish to outreach.results could steer writes by tenant.
findings.recommendation: Treat the muscle's echoed workspace_id as untrusted: derive workspace_id from the lead row by lead_id as the source of truth, and assert the echoed value matches (or ignore it). Defense-in-depth for the tenant boundary.
findings.fix: handle_transition derives workspace_id from the lead row (source of truth) and refuses the transition if the muscle-echoed workspace_id disagrees.

findings.title: lead_id survives intact end-to-end; Rust muscle is a clean opaque metadata passthrough
findings.evidence: Agent-traced all 6 hops: lead_id is a typed Uuid in Rust (models.rs:213, cannot be silently re-minted), the Flink keyer's only fallback is an 'unknown' bucket that process_element discards. The muscle has ZERO correlation_id/workspace_id logic — all 4 result builders in common.rs do `metadata: command.metadata.clone()`, a verbatim echo, so no fork risk originates in Rust. The orchestrator line-109 correlation_id forward is confirmed present and its read-path matches the muscle's write-path.
findings.recommendation: No action. The forks (DATAFLOW-001) are all on the Python side; Rust is clean.

findings.title: transitions-v2 worker is replica-unsafe + auto-commit can silently drop or double-apply lead advancement
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: transition_worker sets enable_auto_commit=True (line 499) and does multi-step non-idempotent work in handle_transition — advances a lead and in _fan_out INSERTs N child leads (lines 275-291). Offset commits on a timer independent of handler completion: a crash mid-handle after commit loses the transition; redelivery after a rebalance re-runs a partial fan-out and DOUBLE-SPAWNS children (the fanout_total guard does not dedupe transition re-entry). Same auto-commit/catch-and-continue root cause as EXEC-001. Must stay replicas:1 until fixed.
findings.recommendation: Switch transitions-v2 to manual commit-after-success (mirror the projector) + make fan-out idempotent on transition id. Keep replicas:1. Folds into the RETRY-THEME failure-policy fix.
findings.fix: transitions-v2 switched to enable_auto_commit=False + commit=True. _fan_out idempotent: a parent already fanned-out at the for_each node is a no-op on redelivery, so a rebalance cannot double-spawn children. Stays replicas:1.

findings.title: dispatcher uses auto_offset_reset='latest' -> intents published before it joins are never dispatched
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: dispatcher.py:161-162 sets enable_auto_commit=True + auto_offset_reset='latest'. On a fresh v2-dispatcher group (or after the group is reset), any intent already on omni.events before the consumer joins is NEVER dispatched -> the lead stalls forever with no command. The muscle (earliest) and projector (earliest) both replay; the dispatcher does not. Combined with auto-commit, a crash between commit and publish_command also drops the command (at-most-once on the command plane). This is a startup/ordering hazard specific to the command plane.
findings.recommendation: Use auto_offset_reset='earliest' for the dispatcher (it's idempotent enough via the muscle's dedupe ledger) and move to manual commit-after-publish. Part of the RETRY-THEME fix.
findings.fix: dispatcher uses auto_offset_reset=earliest + manual commit-after-publish, so intents already on omni.events before the group joins are dispatched.

findings.title: No topic pre-creation; 5 topics rely on Redpanda implicit auto-create at 1 partition
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: neither compose file creates topics or sets partition counts, and the redpanda service has no explicit auto_create_topics_enabled (Redpanda defaults true). omni.events/outreach.commands/results/transitions/dead_letter are created on first produce with 1 partition. Per-tenant ordering is preserved (workspace_id/lead_id keys) but parallelism is capped at 1 consumer/group regardless of replicas — so the dispatcher/muscle replica story is moot until partitions are raised, and a partition's single consumer is a throughput ceiling.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit topic-creation init (rpk topic create with intentional partition counts) so partitioning is a deliberate capacity decision, not a broker default.
findings.fix: Added topics-init service: rpk creates omni.events/outreach.* with intentional partition counts (6/6/6/6/1) instead of 1-partition auto-create.

findings.title: No dependency ordering / readiness gating -> crash-loop churn on cold boot
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: the v2 compose has zero depends_on (its infra db/redpanda lives in another compose project so it can't express it). Python workers call init_pool/init_producer at startup; if db/redpanda aren't up they crash. restart:unless-stopped eventually recovers, but only orchestrator-v2 actually waits (its `until curl jobmanager` loop). The muscle and Python workers have no wait-for-broker/db gate -> noisy crash-loop on every cold start.
findings.recommendation: Add a wait-for-it/healthcheck gate (or retry-with-backoff in init_pool/init_producer) so workers wait for infra instead of crash-looping. Document the cross-project dependency.
findings.fix: init_pool retries with backoff on transient connection errors so cold-boot workers wait for Postgres instead of crash-looping; deterministic auth/catalog errors still fail fast.

findings.title: transitions-v2 is missing MUSCLE_SHARED_SECRET (latent credential-mint failure)
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: backend-v2, dispatcher-v2, muscle-v2 all set MUSCLE_SHARED_SECRET; transitions-v2 does NOT. transitions re-runs node execute() via _fire_node; today the credential-ref mint happens on the dispatcher path so transitions may not need it, but the asymmetry is a latent trap — if a node fired from the transition worker ever needs to mint a credential ref it will silently get muscle_shared_secret='' and fail at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add MUSCLE_SHARED_SECRET to transitions-v2 for consistency, or assert at startup that any worker that can mint credential refs has it set.
findings.fix: transitions-v2 carries MUSCLE_SHARED_SECRET in docker-compose.v2.yml.

findings.title: Plaintext prod secrets committed across both compose files (precise inventory for rotation)
findings.evidence: Agent inventory (key names + file:line, values not printed). docker-compose.v2.yml: DATABASE_URL (21,44,65,90,113), REDIS_URL (22), REDIS_PASSWORD (23), DB_PASSWORD (25,46,92,115), SECRET_KEY (26,47,93,116). docker-compose.yml: Redis --requirepass (20), POSTGRES_PASSWORD (29), DATABASE_URL (43,126,155), REDIS_URL (127), REDIS_PASSWORD (128), DB_PASSWORD (130,157), SECRET_KEY (131,158). Three distinct secret values (DB password, Redis password, SECRET_KEY) committed plaintext in both files. Known rotation target; rotating SECRET_KEY also orphans all Fernet ciphertext (see ENC-001).
findings.recommendation: Move to a .env file (gitignored) or a secret manager; rotate all three values. Sequence the SECRET_KEY rotation with a re-encrypt migration (ENC-001).
findings.fix: Plaintext prod secrets removed from docker-compose.v2.yml: moved to the gitignored .env and referenced via ${VAR}. NOTE: rotate the values previously committed in history.

findings.title: FRONTEND_URL host disagrees with the OAuth redirect hosts baked in config.py
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: backend-v2 sets FRONTEND_URL=https://145-223-21-222.sslip.io:8443 (compose:28) while config.py:60/74/78 bake https://srv1575227.hstgr.cloud/... for the ProductHunt/Google OAuth callbacks. CORS origin and OAuth callback host are two different names — OAuth round-trips only work if both are served and registered in the provider consoles. Same env-host-in-code drift as CFG-002/FE-004.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical external host, drive all of FRONTEND_URL + OAuth redirect URIs from env, and register that one host. Confirm the intended deployment hostname.
findings.fix: OAuth redirect URIs + FRONTEND_URL env-driven (config.py defaults emptied; .env carries FRONTEND_URL); no conflicting hardcoded hosts.

findings.title: Dockerfile.v2 comment contradicts actual nginx wiring (baked, not mounted)
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: the Dockerfile.v2 header (lines 2-3) says the vhost is mounted from frontend/nginx.v2.conf via compose, but the frontend-v2 compose block (148-150) mounts only ./certs and ./acme — nginx.v2.conf is actually COPYed into the image (Dockerfile.v2:21). Editing the nginx config needs a rebuild, not a restart (consistent with the v2-deploy-rebuild rule), but the comment misleads.
findings.recommendation: Fix the comment to state the config is baked at build time and requires a rebuild to change.
findings.fix: Dockerfile.v2 comment corrected: nginx config is BAKED at build time (requires rebuild), not mounted.

findings.title: Consumer groups are unique per worker; required secrets supplied; muscle+projector are replica-safe
findings.evidence: Agent-verified: 5 distinct consumer groups (omni-projector-v1, v2-dispatcher, v2-transitions, muscle-v2, flink-orchestrator) — no two workers share a group, so no message stealing. Both placeholder-rejected required settings (db_password, secret_key) are supplied to all four Python services -> none crash on boot for env reasons. projector-v2 (manual commit after archive+project, idempotent via ON CONFLICT) and muscle-v2 (manual commit + Postgres dedupe ledger, at-least-once) are both replica-safe. The muscle group override avoids colliding with a legacy execution-engine-v2.
findings.recommendation: No action on these. The replica-unsafe ones are dispatcher (DEPLOY-002) and transitions (DEPLOY-001).

findings.title: Projector writes are 100% schema-consistent (zero missing-column / ON CONFLICT / type / NOT NULL bugs)
findings.evidence: Agent column-level cross-check of every INSERT/UPDATE omni_* in the projector against migrations 021-024: every written column exists; every ON CONFLICT target is a real PK/UNIQUE (archive (topic,partition,offset)=UNIQUE 021:247; contacts/companies/deals/leads/messages (id)=PK; lead_scores (lead_id)=PK 022:48; ai_jobs (id)=PK; offsets (topic,partition)=PK 021:264). All NOT-NULL projection columns are supplied or in-code defaulted (companies.name->'Unnamed', deals.name/stage/currency, leads.status, messages.channel). JSONB columns get dict/list via the registered codec (db.py:99-112) — no type mismatch. CHECK constraints (score 0-100, tier, ai kind/status, message direction) are all satisfied by clamped/enumerated writes.
findings.recommendation: No action. The projection layer is the schema-cleanest part of the system.

findings.title: omni_connections.last_refreshed_at is a dead column (never written or read)
findings.evidence: Agent-traced: migration 021:119 creates omni_connections.last_refreshed_at, but integrations.py:81 INSERT omits it and no UPDATE anywhere sets it, and no reader selects it. True dead column on the live path. Only schema-bloat item the column-level cross-check surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Drop the column in a future migration, or wire it (set on connection refresh) if connection-freshness tracking is wanted. Low urgency.
findings.fix: Documented omni_connections.last_refreshed_at as reserved; migration 021 annotated.

findings.title: omni_lead_scores is write-dead — ai.score.completed is never emitted (composes with NODE-001)
findings.evidence: Cross-plane composition of the event-contract + schema audits: _project_lead_score only fires on ai.score.completed, but ai.score never reaches a muscle (NODE-001/CONTRACT-001: node_type ai.score absent from NODE_CHANNEL -> stalls, never runs, never emits ai.score.completed). So the omni_lead_scores table + the AI lead-scoring workstream are write-dead despite the node existing in the palette. The schema is correct (SCHEMA-PROJ-GOOD); it's the upstream node-routing gap that starves it.
findings.recommendation: Resolved by wiring ai.score (CONTRACT-001 fix: node_type->ChannelType + Rust/AI handler emitting ai.score.completed). Until then the lead-scoring product feature does not function on the canvas.

findings.title: Entire Python backend is floor-pinned (>=) with no lockfile -> non-reproducible builds

findings.title: Naukri people-stage e2e fails: company fan-out duplicates + join over-counts + screen verdict not written to child custom_fields
findings.evidence: Live run 2026-06-08 (wf Marketing Agencies India, source.naukri start, lead 345d33d3): naukri scraped OK, 16 ai.screen_company ran (status=sent), but ZERO contacts. DB lineage: parent fanout_total=1 but fanout_done=64; 4 child leads ALL carry the SAME company ('Axis Max Life Insurance') = duplicate fan-out from a max_items:1 for_each; children completed with current_node_id=NULL and custom_fields.screen EMPTY (verdict never written back) so no child could route accept->serper_people. No source.serper_people.requested, no ai.screen_person.queued, no contact.created emitted. Three compounding bugs: (a) for_each spawned duplicate children for one company despite max_items:1; (b) flow.join fanout_done over-counts (64 vs total 1) because many handles route into one join; (c) ai.screen_company verdict (muscle result next_handle) is not persisted onto the child lead's custom_fields.screen, so routing past the screen can't see ACCEPT. Also data: the naukri 'marketing agency' scrape returned an insurance MNC, which the strict ICP prompt would reject anyway.
findings.recommendation: Trace _fan_out child creation (why duplicates for max_items:1) + _join_arrive counter semantics (count distinct children, not arrivals) + ensure the ai_screen result writes decision into the child's custom_fields before routing. Fix on a branch with a local harness, not live prod trial.
findings.fix: Three fixes: (a) _fan_out now _dedup_items() before the max_items cap so a source returning the same company/person twice spawns ONE child, not N (value-keyed, order-preserving). (b) _join_arrive ends the child via an atomic UPDATE...WHERE status<>'completed' RETURNING id and no-ops if not claimed, so a redelivered join-arrival bumps the parent's fanout_done at most once per DISTINCT child (kills the fanout_done=64 vs total=1 over-count that released the barrier early). (c) ai_screen.rs writes the verdict to lead_mutations.custom_fields.screen.{decision,verdict,reason,model} so the screen decision is durable (Leads column + scoring); routing still uses next_handle. Regression tests: test_fan_out_dedups_identical_items, test_join_arrive_counts_distinct_children_idempotently, test_ai_screen_writes_verdict_to_custom_fields. NOTE: the original run's single company was an insurance MNC that Claude correctly REJECTS — a clean re-run needs a real agency in the scrape; the structural bugs that prevented ANY lead are fixed.

findings.title: Source result redelivered N× -> fan-out reads pre-mutation snapshot (fanout_total=0 with companies present)
findings.evidence: After E2E-001 fix, run #3 (lead 76cf19e5): naukri scraped 35 companies (custom_fields.companies len=35) but parent ended fanout_total=0, status=active, ZERO children. transitions log shows FOUR 'fan_out skipped: already claimed/fanned (redelivery/concurrent)' — so the source.naukri RESULT was delivered ~5× to the transition worker. The atomic claim (E2E-001) correctly blocked the 4 dup waves (the 20-dupe bug IS fixed), but the ONE delivery that won the claim ran _fan_out against a parent snapshot whose custom_fields.companies mutation had not landed (or it claimed before _apply_lead_mutations of its own delivery committed), so items=[] -> fanout_total=0 and no children. Root cause: the source-command RESULT is not deduped (at-least-once redelivery of the naukri ExecutionResult) AND the claim+read-items sequence is not serialized with the company-list mutation apply. Result: a successful scrape produces zero leads intermittently.
findings.recommendation: (1) Dedupe the source result by command_id in the muscle->results consumer (processed_commands ledger) so one scrape => one transition. (2) In _fan_out, read custom_fields fresh from the DB INSIDE the claim transaction (not from the passed-in snapshot), so the company list is read-after-write consistent with the mutation. Build + verify on a branch with a deterministic harness (simulate N concurrent deliveries) — NOT by re-running live paid scrapes.
findings.fix: _fan_out now re-reads custom_fields FRESH from the DB immediately after winning the atomic claim (read-after-write), instead of trusting the passed-in transition snapshot. The claim serializes us and each delivery applies its own mutation before routing, so the committed row always has the collection — fanout_total can no longer be 0 when companies are present. Proven by a deterministic asyncio concurrency harness (audit/tests/test_fanout_concurrency.py): (1) 5 concurrent/redelivered fan-outs spawn exactly ONE wave of 5 children (not 20); (2) a STALE empty snapshot still yields 3 children by reading the DB's committed 3 companies. The harness reproduces BOTH the 20-dupe (E2E-001) and 0-children (E2E-002) symptoms and confirms the fixes without paid live runs. FOLLOW-UP (lower priority, not blocking): dedupe the source ExecutionResult by command_id at the Flink results layer so one scrape => one transition (the read-after-write fix already makes redelivery harmless).
